overview: This 258-page file traces U.S. complaints and diplomatic inquiries about Japanese trade marks, copied products, and misleading claims of American origin in the 1930s. Cases involving Edison lamps, PARAFLOW oil marks, and Parker pens show how officials investigated alleged infringement, weighed Japanese law and treaty remedies, and often directed companies toward private legal action.
interest: Case correspondence and translated Japanese laws reveal the evidence and legal limits shaping U.S. responses to alleged infringement.
